newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian palm oil prices steady, supply tight.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian palm oil prices steady, supply tight.

text.p: Indonesian crude palm oil and olein prices remained steady despite possible imports of cooking oil by the government, traders said.
They said tight supply of crude palm oil (CPO) in the domestic market continued to linger on the supply side and kept an upbeat tone on market prices.
CPO, which was last tendered at 1,222.5 rupiah/kg in Medan last week, was now offered at 1,240 rupiah/kg. But traders said nothing was traded so far.
One trader in Medan said the tight CPO market had also caused the olein market to sustain its high price.
"Reports of possible purchases (of cooking oil) by the government dampened the market only briefly in the morning," the trader said.
He said traders seemed to expect the condition to continue until September on carry-forward effect from August.
"We anticipate the government will announce a higher export tax in September which should stabilise the situation by the end of next month," the trader said.
Ready palm olein was quoted at 1,600 rupiah/kg in Java and 1,510 rupiah in Medan. Some traders said olein for September delivery was quoted at 1,560 rupiah/kg in Jakarta.
